application.name: ofetch (unjs)
application.summary: Source of the `ofetch` library (evidenced by the `"ofetch"` import in examples/type-safety.ts and the demo URL `https://ungh.cc/repos/unjs/ofetch`). It is a TypeScript HTTP-client utility — a "smart fetch" wrapper — not an end-user application. It wraps native `fetch` (or a Node.js polyfill) with automatic JSON body serialization, content-type-aware response parsing, retries, timeouts, lifecycle hooks, baseURL/query merging, and a normalized `FetchError`. Consumers import `ofetch`/`$fetch` (src/index.ts universal, src/node.ts Node) or build custom instances via `createFetch(...).create()`.
application.purpose: Provide a universal, DX-friendly fetch client with predictable error handling and typed responses.

domains.name: Request pipeline orchestration
domains.description: createFetch builds a $fetch instance whose internal raw-fetch closure runs the full pipeline: option resolution, URL/baseURL/query handling, body serialization, hooks, native fetch call, response parsing, error/retry handling.

domains.name: Error normalization & retry policy
domains.description: onError decides whether to retry (retry count, retryStatusCodes, retryDelay, abort detection) or throw a normalized FetchError built by createFetchError.

domains.name: Request option resolution
domains.description: resolveFetchOptions merges per-request options with instance defaults: headers (mergeHeaders) and query/params objects.

domains.name: Body serialization & response parsing
domains.description: isJSONSerializable / isPayloadMethod drive auto JSON.stringify of request bodies; detectResponseType picks json/text/blob parsing by Content-Type; JSON parsed safely via the destr dependency.

domains.name: Runtime adaptation
domains.description: src/index.ts targets global fetch/Headers/AbortController; src/node.ts falls back to node-fetch-native with optional HTTP(S) keep-alive agents.

domains.name: Developer experience & testing
domains.description: Typed-response example, manual playground script, and vitest integration tests against a local h3/listhen server.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Demo script showing typed usage: fetches repo metadata from ungh.cc and logs name/stars of a strongly typed Repo object.

Core factory producing the $fetch client. Its calls (resolveFetchOptions, callHooks, isPayloadMethod, isJSONSerializable, detectResponseType, onError) execute inside its internal $fetchRaw pipeline; the self-call createFetch→createFetch powers `$fetch.create()` for derived instances with merged defaults. Also defines $fetch.raw and $fetch.native (not graph entities).

Retry/error handler: detects user aborts (AbortError without timeout → no retry), applies default retry counts via isPayloadMethod, waits per retryDelay, retries by re-invoking the internal raw fetch, otherwise builds and throws the normalized error via createFetchError.

Constructs the FetchError: message pattern `[METHOD] "url": <status statusText> <message>` (validated by tests), attaches request/options/response and data/status/statusCode/statusText getters from the context.
Merges request options with instance defaults — headers via mergeHeaders, and query/params into one combined object.
Combines request-level and default HeadersInit values into a single Headers instance (input wins over defaults).
Invokes a lifecycle hook or an array of hooks sequentially, awaiting each.
Identifies body-carrying methods (PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE); used to gate body serialization and to set default retry count (0 for payload methods, 1 otherwise).
Decides if a request body can be auto-JSON-stringified (primitives, arrays, plain objects, toJSON); excludes Buffer-like, streams, FormData, etc.
Chooses response parser from Content-Type: JSON_RE → json, text-ish/SVG/XML/HTML → text, else blob; empty content-type defaults to json.
Node runtime adapter: returns node-fetch-native directly, or a keep-alive-enabled wrapper (http/https Agents) when FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE env var is true.
Manual playground script hitting http://httpstat.us/500 to observe error behavior; exits with code 1 on error.
Test helper for the 'abort with retry' case: aborts an AbortController, then calls $fetch with retry and the aborted signal, expecting rejection.

applicationFacts: Dual entry points: src/index.ts (universal, uses globalThis fetch/Headers/AbortController; rejects with '[ofetch] global.fetch is not supported!' when unavailable) and src/node.ts (falls back to node-fetch-native, optional keep-alive). Confirmed by build.config.ts entries ["src/index", "src/node"].
Build tooling: unbuild with declarations, CJS emitted via rollup, `undici` marked external (build.config.ts).
Auto JSON requests: payload-method bodies that are JSON-serializable are stringified, and content-type/accept headers default to application/json unless already set.

Response parsing: JSON bodies parsed with destr unless options.parseResponse is provided; responseType option forces json/text/blob/arrayBuffer/stream; null-body statuses (101, 204, 205, 304) and HEAD requests skip body parsing.
Error policy: HTTP 400–599 triggers onResponseError then onError unless ignoreResponseError is set; the thrown error carries parsed response data (error.data).
Retry policy: default 0 retries for payload methods, 1 for others; retries only when status is in retryStatusCodes; retryDelay is a number or a context callback; user aborts are never auto-retried.
Timeout implementation creates its own AbortController and synthesizes a TimeoutError (name 'TimeoutError', code 23) when the timer fires.

Test suite (test/index.test.ts) spins up a local h3 app via listhen with routes /ok, /params, /url, /echo, /post, /binary, /403, /408, /204, /timeout and exercises hooks, retries, timeouts, aborts, body types (FormData, URLSearchParams, ReadableStream, Readable, Buffer), and default-option merging.
Vitest coverage reporters configured: text, clover, json (vitest.config.ts).
